annotation.title_clean: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Regulations (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems): SOR/2019-11
annotation.title_en: Regulations Amending the Canadian Aviation Regulations (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems): SOR/2019-11
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Governor General in Council / Transport Canada (Minister of Transport)
annotation.venue: Canada Gazette, Part II, Vol. 153, No. 1
annotation.summary_en: Canadian regulations adding Part IX to the Canadian Aviation Regulations governing drones of 250 g to 25 kg flown within visual line of sight. They require registration, pilot certification, manufacturer safety declarations, and operating limits, and replace many special flight operations certificates. A Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement gives the cost-benefit analysis.
key_provisions_or_claims: Mandatory registration of RPAs 250 g–25 kg; pilots must be 14+ (basic) or 16+ (advanced) and certified by exam
Basic vs advanced operations tiers based on proximity to people, controlled airspace and airports
Manufacturers self-declare compliance with Standard 922 for advanced operations
Operating limits: 400 ft AGL, visual line of sight, no autonomous systems without immediate control, payload restrictions
Special Flight Operations Certificates for BVLOS and other higher-risk ops; administrative monetary penalties up to $5,000/$25,000
